The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $cot⁡\theta .$
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/5284ae5a30a5d370d52c887cc6222ee4991a98d087dc751cbcfe5d7307ca1d47.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $sin⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}sin⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{17}{81}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{64}{81}} \\  & =\pm \frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $sin⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $sin⁡\theta =\frac{8}{9}.$

Finally, knowing that $cot⁡\theta =\frac{cos⁡\theta }{sin⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
cot⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9})}{(\frac{8}{9})}=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{8}.
$$
